Seminar Title:

Social Audit and Accounting as Pathways to Sustainable Corporate Social Responsibility: A Study in an Indian State

Abstract:

India, with a population of 1.4 billion, aims to become a developed nation by 2047, requiring responsible corporate engagement. Despite substantial CSR investments, many initiatives face challenges in effectiveness and sustainability. To address these issues, the present study develops and empirically validates a Sustainable Corporate Social Responsibility (SCSR) framework designed to guide policymakers and corporate decision-makers in implementing CSR programs that effectively tackle societal challenges while generating lasting value for organizations. This study examines the roles of Social Audit (SA) and Social Accounting (SAC) in promoting SCSR, with the mediating influence of Corporate Social Innovation (CSI), Inclusive Growth (IG), and Creating Shared Value (CSV), and the moderating role of Community Participation (CP) in achieving sustainable development outcomes. Through this integrated framework, this study provides deeper insights into how accountability mechanisms, innovative social practices, and stakeholder engagement collectively contribute to achieving sustainable and impactful CSR outcomes. For the present study, we have collected responses from the ground-level CSR beneficiaries based in Odisha, India. For collecting responses, we employed the purposive sampling method. A total of 600 questionnaires were administered for this study, out of which 409 were deemed valid for analysis, resulting in a response rate of 68.17%. Factor analysis and linear regression techniques were applied to validate the constructs and explore preliminary associations, while Structural Equation Modeling was used to test the hypothesized framework.&nbsp The findings indicate that both SA and SAC have a positive effect on SCSR. Additionally, results suggest that CSI partially mediates the relationship between SA and SCSR, while IG and CSV partially mediate the relationships between CSI and SCSR, as well as SAC and SCSR. Furthermore, the results show that CP moderates the relationship between CSI and SCSR. This study offers a novel perspective on CSR implementation, highlighting how accountability mechanisms, innovative social practices, and stakeholder engagement collectively drive sustainable and impactful CSR outcomes. It provides a foundation for improving CSR execution and offers directions for future research in auditing, accounting, social innovation, and sustainable corporate responsibility.

Keywords: Social Audit Social Accounting Corporate Social Innovation Inclusive Growth Creating Shared Value Sustainable Corporate Social Responsibility
